title: Chapter 23: Real Killer
html:
He raced to the window and looked down.

That’s higher than I thought.Footsteps thundered closer behind him. Whatever route he chose, he had only seconds to decide.

With the others closing in, Chen Ge escaped through the window and dropped to the lower level, landing hard but managing to keep moving.

“He saw what we were doing!”

“Don’t let him get away!”

The landlord appeared at the doorway, furious. “You think you can run?”

Chen Ge scrambled away from the building. His clothes snagged as he descended, but he ignored the scrapes and kept going.

Shouts followed him into the yard. Something struck the ground nearby, and the sound was enough to make him run even faster.

If they catch me, I’m in serious trouble.

The front door opened and the remaining tenants joined the pursuit.

“You people are unbelievable!” Chen Ge sprinted for the edge of the property. Beyond it lay a dense forest. He could barely see where he was going, but staying near the building was no longer an option, so he plunged among the trees.

Flashlight beams occasionally cut through the darkness behind him, accompanied by angry shouts. Chen Ge did not look back. He had only one thought: keep moving.

Branches caught at his clothes and mud clung to his shoes. After running until his lungs burned, he finally realized the voices behind him had grown distant.

He crouched behind a thicket and watched faint lights move far away. Pressing one hand to the ground, he struggled to catch his breath.

That was far too close.One bad decision inside the building could have ended very differently.

The difficulty of this Trial Mission is ridiculous.The black phone’s missions seemed determined to drag him into situations that no sane game designer would consider reasonable—and unlike a game, the consequences here were real.

Losing the landlord’s group did not mean he was safe. Chen Ge remained hidden, half-expecting a flashlight beam to appear through the trees at any moment.

Once his heartbeat settled, he carefully emerged from cover. The distant lights had vanished. The forest was so quiet that he could not even hear birds.

Which way gets me out of here?He had to admit that he was completely lost.Do I wait here until morning?

Chen Ge checked his phone and discovered that the livestream was still running. The screen had been dark for more than an hour, and the chat was now filled with confused question marks. Even the regular viewers had no idea what kind of stream they were watching anymore.

He had no time to explain. He glanced at a message from He San, but before he could open it, leaves rustled somewhere behind him.

Chen Ge immediately dimmed the phone and went still, listening intently in the direction of the sound.

A moment later, a weak beam of light passed between the trees.

Then a familiar voice called, “Is someone there? Who is it?”

Wang Qi? Didn’t he leave the apartments hours ago? What is he doing out here in the middle of the night?Curious as he was, Chen Ge knew better than to announce himself. He stayed hidden.

Did I imagine it? No. That was definitely his voice.Wang Qi swept his flashlight across the area and wandered nearby.

I can’t let him see me. There is something seriously wrong with his story.Rather than reveal himself, Chen Ge retreated farther into the trees.

After moving for some time, he noticed the slope growing steeper. He had apparently circled around to the opposite side of the hill.

Beyond a dense patch of brush stood a secluded wooden cabin surrounded by trees. A weathered sign on the door carried a standard forest-safety notice warning visitors to prevent fires and avoid littering.

This looks like some kind of ranger shelter.He tested the door. It was unlocked. As it creaked open, an odd smell drifted from inside.

What is that?He kept his phone light low as he looked around.

The cabin was small but crammed with everyday objects, as though someone had been using it as both a home and a dumping ground.

Following the strange smell, Chen Ge reached a simple bed. Beneath it he found a pile of old, damp clothing.

A hoarder?The discovery became stranger when he realized all the clothes appeared to belong to the same young woman. They were worn, unwashed, and roughly the same size.

Some of this mud is still fresh. These clothes were used recently.

His experience with costume design and Mortician’s Makeup had trained his eye for body proportions. Looking at the clothes, he remembered the figure concealed in the apartment wall.

The size looks right. These could have belonged to her.

But if so, why were her clothes hidden in this cabin—and why did some of them look recently handled?

His pulse quickened. Several scraps of paper were pinned or tucked among the clothes, each carrying the same simple declaration: “I love you.”

That handwriting…Chen Ge compared the notes with the messages he had taken from the dolls. The handwriting looked almost identical.

The dolls are years old, but these clothes were brought here much more recently. Why do the messages look like they came from the same person?

The same handwriting and the same declarations of love suggested that both discoveries might be connected.

As Chen Ge moved the clothes, a phone in a pink case slipped from one of the pockets.

A phone?

He picked it up. The screen was already open to a draft message, as though someone had been typing just before it was abandoned.

“Save me”?

A chill ran through him. He checked the message history and found the same two words repeated again and again: Save me.
